title: Trans Resveratrol Powder | Micronised | 99% Purity | 5* Trustpilot
abstract:
**Interactions:** Resveratrol is known to inhibit members of the Cytochrome P450 class of enzymes. As a result, it may interfere with antiplatelet and anticoagulant medications such as Warfarin. Additionally, resveratrol is classed as a phytoestrogen, a plant molecule that can mimic the effects of oestrogen in the body. Therefore, individuals who are hormone replacement therapies should therefore consult with their doctors before adding resveratrol to their longevity protocols. If you are taking these medications or any other medication, please first speak with your doctor before adding Resveratrol to your supplement regime.  
For further information regarding any other potential drug and supplement interactions of Resveratrol please see the ingredient profile on Drug Bank.*  
**Allergy:** This product does not contain any common allergens; however, it should not be used by anyone with a history of hypersensitivity to its ingredients or those taking medications that may interact with it.  
**Pregnancy:** If pregnant, consult your health professional before using this product.  
\*Drug Bank is an independent website that lists potential interactions between the ingredients in Trans-Resvertrol and other medications and supplements. It may not, however, list all known possible interactions. If you are on any medications or supplements you feel may interact negatively with Trans-Resvertrol please first speak with your doctor before using this product.
Dosage: 5 mg/kg/day and 45 mg/kg/day resveratrol for 8 weeks
Outcome: Resveratrol improved bone density and promoted autophagy in bone cells through SIRT1 activation.
Summary: High-dose resveratrol activated SIRT1 and enhanced mitophagy in osteoblasts, protecting against bone loss in osteoporosis rats.  
*\*Sirtuin 1 is a molecule that when activated has been shown to increase lifespan in both cell and mouse studies. While Resveratrol is believed to work by activating this molecule there is still [debate](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15684413/) in the longevity community about its efficacy of this.*  
**Resveratrol Improves Health and Survival of Mice on a High-Calorie Diet** – Preclinical Animal Study  
Dosage: Resveratrol (dosage not specified)
Outcome: Increased lifespan and improved health markers in mice fed a high-calorie diet
Summary: In middle-aged mice, resveratrol improved general health and increased lifespan, mimicking the benefits of a standard diet. This was noted through several markers including better insulin sensitivity, lower levels of certain ageing-related factors, more mitochondria (energy-producing structures in cells) and enhanced physical ability.  
**Small molecule activators of sirtuins extend Saccharomyces cerevisiae lifespan** – Cell Study  
Dosage: Resveratrol, a compound found in red wine
Outcome: Extended lifespan of yeast by 70%
Summary: Resveratrol, known for its antioxidant properties, may help treat rheumatoid arthritis by reducing inflammation and protecting joints. Research suggests it could complement existing RA treatments, though more studies are needed to confirm its effectiveness and determine optimal dosages.  
**Effect of Resveratrol Supplementation on Inflammatory Markers –** A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomised Controlled Trials  
Dosage: Mixed
Outcome: Reduction in levels of TNF-α and hs-CRP, two markers of inflammation
Summary: This study found that taking resveratrol can help lower certain signs of inflammation in the body. This suggests resveratrol might be useful alongside other treatments for diseases linked to inflammation.  
Resveratrol is a natural plant flavonoid found in red wine, grape skins, berries, and plants like Japanese Knotweed, a common supplement source. It is produced by plants in response to stress, injury, or pathogens as part of their defence system.  
Micronised reseveratrol has been shown in one [study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3173869/) to be up to 3.6 times more bioavailable than standard resveratrol.
